name: The Old Course, St Andrews
blurb: The original. Seven double greens, the Road Hole and the Swilcan Bridge; every golfer should walk up the 18th once.

name: Carnoustie Championship
blurb: Across the Tay from St Andrews and the hardest Open venue there is. The Barry Burn finish has decided championships.

name: Royal Troon
blurb: Nine-time Open host on the Ayrshire coast, home of the Postage Stamp, the most famous short par 3 in golf.

name: Turnberry, Ailsa
blurb: The most beautiful links in Scotland, with the lighthouse, Ailsa Craig and the Duel in the Sun holes along the shore.

name: Muirfield
blurb: The Honourable Company's links in East Lothian: two loops, every wind direction, and a visitor day that is worth planning a trip around.

name: Kingsbarns
blurb: Modern links on the coast south of St Andrews with the sea on almost every hole. Opened in 2000 and already a classic.

name: Royal Dornoch
blurb: Far north in the Highlands and worth every mile. Natural links, plateau greens and gorse in flower in May.

name: North Berwick, West Links
blurb: Quirky, historic and enormous fun, with the original Redan hole and the Bass Rock out to sea.

name: Cabot Highlands (Castle Stuart)
blurb: Scottish Open venue above the Moray Firth near Inverness, wide fairways and views to the Black Isle.

name: Gleneagles, King's Course
blurb: James Braid's inland masterpiece in Perthshire, with the hotel to match. The 2014 Ryder Cup was played on the neighbouring PGA Centenary.
